### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
Hydro buffers have variable, x3, x2, x1 axes.
NMASS default 0; exterior slabs default true.
Order: code map; no independent measured convergence order.
No defining equation: this section maps control flow or data ownership.
:::

Hydro buffers have variable, x3, x2, x1 axes. A resolved direction includes ghosts on both sides; a one-cell direction
has no ghost storage. Primitive and conserved row meanings differ even though their row indices agree.

### Derivation

No separate derivation: this section describes an interface or control-flow path. Numerical operators are derived in
their owning chapters.

### Numerical method

Cell values occupy the final three axes; x1 is contiguous in the nominal layout. The first species row follows energy
or pressure. At a face the left and right reconstruction slots share the face index; `_apply_inplace` offsets their
output slices by one. `part` takes offsets in x3, x2, x1 order, returning an interior or boundary slab with optional
extensions and depth. In the Code table, `il` and `iu` are the first and last interior math indices, not new physical
variables. Layout has no convergence order.

@fig-ch01-layout-flow shows the data or call sequence.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch01-layout-flow
#| fig-cap: "A lower-wall storage stencil. Blue circles are cell averages, orange triangles are face states, the hatched cell is a ghost and the thick black line is the physical wall. The shared face index holds both reconstructed states."
#| fig-alt: "Cells i-1, i and i+1, with i-1 a ghost and the wall at face i-1/2."
```

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
NMASS greater than zero is rejected by the species-layout static assertion. Degenerate axes cannot supply an ordinary
multi-cell stencil. The tests here exercise selected shapes and slabs rather than every depth/extension combination.
:::
